name: St Gallen PAE trial
aliases: PAE versus TURP (St Gallen Cantonal Hospital)
question: Is prostatic artery embolisation noninferior to TURP for relieving symptoms in men with medically refractory BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms?

arms.label: Prostatic artery embolisation (PAE) with 250–400 µm microspheres
monopolar transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP)

design.population: Men aged 40 or older with medically refractory BPH-related LUTS (IPSS 8 or higher, Qmax below 12 mL/s or retention) and a 25 to 80 mL prostate who were candidates for TURP; 99 of 103 randomized were treated.
design.locator: Methods, Participants and Randomisation; Results, Study patients (arm sizes of 51 and 52 derived: 48 and 51 analyzed plus 3 and 1 post-randomization exclusions)

verdictNote: Noninferiority not shown: 12-week IPSS difference of 1.54 points favored TURP, upper confidence limit 4.52 exceeded the 3-point margin.
takeaway: Prostatic artery embolisation was compared with monopolar TURP in 103 randomized men with refractory BPH symptoms: 12-week IPSS fell 9.23 versus 10.77 points, but noninferiority within the 3-point margin was not shown (95% CI −1.45 to 4.52), and TURP improved flow and obstruction more.

reports.label: Primary report (12-week outcomes)
reports.citation: Abt D, Hechelhammer L, Müllhaupt G, et al. "Comparison of prostatic artery embolisation (PAE) versus transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia: randomised, open label, non-inferiority trial." *BMJ.* 2018;361:k2338. doi:10.1136/bmj.k2338
reports.followUp: 12 weeks (primary endpoint); per-protocol analysis of 48 PAE and 51 TURP patients

results.measure: Mean change in IPSS from baseline to 12 weeks, per protocol (PAE minus TURP; positive favors TURP)
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin: a between-group difference below 3 points (one-sided t test, alpha 0.025). The baseline-adjusted analysis gave a difference of 2.87 points (95% CI 0.53 to 5.21; noninferiority P=0.46). 48 PAE and 51 TURP patients analyzed. The standard deviation of the IPSS change was 7.5 points, against 4.6 assumed in the sample size calculation (Discussion).

harms.label: Treatment-related adverse events, total events in first 12 weeks
harms.note: Events, not patients; postoperative pain and ejaculatory disorders were assessed separately and not counted. P=0.003.

harms.label: At least one treatment-related adverse event
harms.note: Relative risk after PAE 0.89 (95% CI 0.67 to 1.17; P=0.52). 48 PAE and 51 TURP patients.

harms.label: Two or more treatment-related adverse events
harms.note: Relative risk after PAE 0.37 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.75; P=0.005).

harms.label: Clavien grade 1 / 2 / 3 as a share of adverse events
harms.note: Distribution across severity classes did not differ (P=0.44).

harms.label: Postoperative pain during hospital stay
harms.note: Relative risk 1.76 (95% CI 1.08 to 2.87; P=0.03). Denominators are not given in the text.

harms.label: Severe postoperative pain (VAS 6 or higher)
harms.note: 9 PAE patients; limited to the first 12 to 24 hours. Relative risk 4.41 (95% CI 1.00 to 19.33; P=0.06).

harms.label: Ejaculatory dysfunction among patients with assessable ejaculation
harms.note: Relative risk 0.67 (95% CI 0.45 to 0.98); the report gives P=0.06.

harms.label: Angiointervention-specific complications after PAE
harms.note: One moderate puncture-site hematoma, one postembolization syndrome with fever lasting under 24 hours, and one limited bladder-wall ischemia that required transurethral removal of necrotic tissue. One patient reported de novo erectile dysfunction.

delivery.label: PAE technique
delivery.value: Right common femoral access; selective internal iliac arteriography with a 5 F catheter; prostatic arteries catheterized with 1.9 to 2.4 F microcatheters and embolized with 250 to 400 µm Embozene microspheres, bilaterally if possible; cone beam CT in challenging anatomy.
delivery.note: A single experienced interventional radiologist performed all embolizations. Success was defined as loss of the normal prostatic blush and complete stasis of flow in the prostatic arteries. A 16 F catheter was placed before the procedure and removed the morning after.

delivery.label: TURP technique
delivery.value: Monopolar TURP with a 24 F resectoscope, 180 W cutting and 60 W coagulation, tungsten loop and mannitol-sorbitol irrigation; 20 F three-way catheter for at least 2 days.
delivery.note: Four experienced study physicians performed TURP.

delivery.label: Procedure time
delivery.note: P<0.001. TURP resection time 58.25 min (SD 24.33); resected tissue weight 25.20 g (SD 15.16).

delivery.label: PAE fluoroscopy time, dose-area product and embolic volume
delivery.value: Fluoroscopy 50.8 min (SD 17.5); dose-area product 176.5 Gy·cm² (SD 101.2); 1.0 mL (SD 0.4) of microspheres.
delivery.note: Unit printed as Gy/cm2 in the table.

delivery.label: Post-randomization exclusions
delivery.value: Four of 103 randomized patients were not analyzed: 2 allocated to PAE and 1 to TURP refused surgery, and PAE was not possible in 1 patient because of vascular disease.
delivery.note: That patient later had laser vaporization. All 48 PAE and 51 TURP patients treated per randomization attended the 12-week visit.
